title: Light as electromagnetic radiation
core_concept: Light consists of propagating electromagnetic fields that transport energy and momentum.
assumptions_or_caveats: Electromagnetic waves propagate through vacuum; λ is vacuum wavelength and f is frequency.
microscopy_relevance: Foundational to optical illumination and imaging.

title: How objects become visible
core_concept: A source illuminates an object; some reflected or scattered light reaches an observer or detector.
assumptions_or_caveats: Absorption, transmission and scattering determine observed contrast.
microscopy_relevance: Explains image formation at the most basic level.

title: Electric and magnetic fields
core_concept: An electromagnetic plane wave has transverse electric and magnetic fields mutually perpendicular to propagation.
assumptions_or_caveats: Ideal plane-wave model; tightly focused beams can contain longitudinal field components.
microscopy_relevance: Polarization and focusing matter in microscopy.

title: Vacuum propagation
core_concept: Electromagnetic waves need no material medium; sound waves do.
assumptions_or_caveats: c is the exact vacuum speed of light; speed in matter depends on optical properties.
microscopy_relevance: Establishes the meaning of vacuum wavelength.

title: Maxwell's unification
core_concept: Maxwell's equations link electric and magnetic fields and predict propagating electromagnetic waves.
assumptions_or_caveats: The expression applies to classical electromagnetic waves in vacuum.
microscopy_relevance: Provides the classical foundation for microscope optics.

title: Wavelength and frequency
core_concept: Wavelength is spatial periodicity; frequency is cycles per second.
assumptions_or_caveats: Use vacuum wavelength for c; in a medium phase velocity and wavelength change while frequency is conserved across a stationary interface.

title: Electromagnetic spectrum
core_concept: Radio, infrared, visible, ultraviolet and X-rays are all electromagnetic radiation.
assumptions_or_caveats: Human visibility covers only a limited wavelength interval.
microscopy_relevance: Near-infrared light is commonly used in multiphoton excitation.

title: Photon concept
core_concept: A photon is a quantum excitation of the electromagnetic field, not a classical miniature ball.
assumptions_or_caveats: Photon detections can be discrete while interference remains observable.
microscopy_relevance: Needed to understand molecular absorption and emission.

title: Photon energy versus intensity
core_concept: Photon energy is determined by frequency; optical intensity measures energy flow per unit area.
assumptions_or_caveats: Higher intensity need not mean higher energy per photon.
microscopy_relevance: Separates excitation wavelength from excitation power.

title: Poynting vector
core_concept: Electromagnetic energy flux density is described by the Poynting vector.
assumptions_or_caveats: E in V/m; H in A/m; S in W/m².
microscopy_relevance: Connects electromagnetic fields with illumination energy delivery.

title: Field amplitude and intensity
core_concept: For a monochromatic plane wave in vacuum, time-averaged intensity scales with squared peak electric-field amplitude.
assumptions_or_caveats: Requires ideal plane-wave assumptions; doubling E0 quadruples intensity.

title: Wave and quantum descriptions
core_concept: Wave optics explains propagation and interference; quantum optics describes photon states and discrete interactions.
assumptions_or_caveats: Neither classical waves nor tiny-ball pictures explain all light phenomena.
microscopy_relevance: Choose the physical model appropriate to the question.

title: Molecular fluorescence
core_concept: Suitable molecules absorb excitation energy, relax, and may emit photons at characteristic wavelengths.
assumptions_or_caveats: Absorption does not guarantee fluorescence; nonradiative relaxation can occur.

title: Two-photon energy equivalence
core_concept: Two photons at 1064.8 nm carry approximately 2.329 eV, equal to one photon at 532.4 nm.
assumptions_or_caveats: Energy equivalence does not imply equal selection rules or excitation efficiency.

title: Scope and limitations
core_concept: Classical electromagnetism predicts many optical properties, while quantized molecular states govern optical transitions.
assumptions_or_caveats: Real microscope beams are focused, often pulsed and affected by dispersion and aberrations.
microscopy_relevance: Combining classical and quantum models is essential for multiphoton microscopy.
